The statement conveys a cautiously optimistic stance: the labor market is strengthening and growth remains moderate, prompting a 25 bp hike to a 0.75–1.00% target range while maintaining an accommodative posture via reinvestments. This “gradualism” is consistent with estimated inertial policy rules in the New Keynesian framework (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and with forecast-targeting principles that move rates as inflation converges to target (Svensson and Woodford). Implementation via interest on reserves and the ON RRP facility aligns with operating-procedure insights in Goodfriend (2002). Continued reinvestment to keep longer-term yields low reflects term-structure evidence that policy affects risk premia and expectations beyond the short rate (Cochrane and Piazzesi) and is consistent with QE transmission literature. With market-based inflation compensation still low and one dissent preferring no hike, the tone is positive but measured rather than overtly hawkish.
